# package ethernetip

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip"
```

Package ethernetip is the module root of a pure Go implementation of EtherNet/IP and the Common Industrial Protocol (CIP), the industrial Ethernet protocol of ODVA used by programmable controllers, I/O adapters, drives and sensors.

Applications import the subpackages:

  - [github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/client): the originator of explicit messages: sessions, unconnected and connected (Class 3) messaging, Forward\_Open and Forward\_Close, routing through Unconnected\_Send, Multiple Service Packet, discovery with ListIdentity
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/scanner](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/scanner): the originator of Class 1 (and Class 0) implicit I/O connections: cyclic UDP exchange with sequence handling, run/idle, timeouts and recovery
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/server](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/server): the target (adapter): the Message Router with the Identity, Message Router, Assembly, Connection Manager, Port, TCP/IP Interface and Ethernet Link objects, explicit and implicit connections, user-defined objects
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/logix](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/logix): Rockwell Automation Logix extensions (vendor specific, not CIP): symbolic tag reads and writes, fragmentation, tag lists, templates and UDTs; on the client and, emulated, on the server
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/eds](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/eds): Electronic Data Sheets: parser, validation, writer and the Go code generator behind ethernetipctl eds
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/cip](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/cip): the CIP codec: data types, EPATHs, messages, the Connection Manager services, the catalog of codes
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/encap](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/encap): the encapsulation codec: headers, commands, the common packet format
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/implicit](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/implicit): the codec and the UDP endpoint of implicit (I/O) messages, shared by scanner and server

This package holds what they share: the sentinel and typed errors, the [Logger](#type-logger) and [Metrics](#type-metrics) interfaces and the [State](#type-state) of sessions and connections.

Docs: README.md, API.md (public API), ARCHITECTURE.md, ERRORS.md (error semantics), OBSERVABILITY.md (logging and metrics), INTEROPERABILITY.md (coverage and interop results), SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CATALOG.md (codes and their provenance), RELEASE.md (changelog).

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrClosed reports an operation on a client, connection or server that
	// was closed by the application.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("ethernetip: closed")

	// ErrNotConnected reports a request on a client that has no registered
	// session.
	ErrNotConnected = errors.New("ethernetip: not connected")

	// ErrConnectFailed reports that a client could not establish its
	// session: the dial, the TLS handshake or RegisterSession failed. The
	// underlying error is wrapped alongside it.
	ErrConnectFailed = errors.New("ethernetip: connect failed")

	// ErrConnectionLost reports that the peer closed the TCP connection or
	// the transport failed while a request was in progress.
	ErrConnectionLost = errors.New("ethernetip: connection lost")

	// ErrTimeout reports that the peer did not answer within the request
	// timeout, or that an I/O connection's consumed data stopped arriving
	// within its connection timeout.
	ErrTimeout = errors.New("ethernetip: timeout")

	// ErrProtocol reports a peer that violated the protocol: a malformed
	// encapsulation packet or CIP response, a reply to a service that was
	// not requested, an unexpected item in a common packet format.
	ErrProtocol = errors.New("ethernetip: protocol violation")

	// ErrSession reports an encapsulation level failure of the session: the
	// peer rejected the session handle, the protocol version or the
	// command. An *[EncapError] carries the status.
	ErrSession = errors.New("ethernetip: session error")

	// ErrBusy reports a request that cannot be issued because a limit was
	// reached: pending requests of a client, sessions or connections of a
	// server.
	ErrBusy = errors.New("ethernetip: resource limit reached")

	// ErrUnsupported reports that the peer does not support the service or
	// attribute (CIP general status 0x08 or 0x14), or that the operation is
	// not available on this transport.
	ErrUnsupported = errors.New("ethernetip: unsupported")

	// ErrInvalidOption reports an option or argument value a client, scanner
	// or server cannot be constructed or called with.
	ErrInvalidOption = errors.New("ethernetip: invalid option")
)
```

Sentinel errors shared by the client, the scanner and the server. They are usually wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is.

## Types

### type CIPError

```go
type CIPError struct {
	// Service is the service code of the request (without the reply bit).
	Service cip.Service
	// Path is the request path, for messages; it may be nil.
	Path cip.Path
	// Status is the general status code.
	Status cip.GeneralStatus
	// Extended is the additional status, in the order sent.
	Extended []uint16
	// Data is the response data that came with the error, if any. Some
	// services return data with an error (Forward_Open's remaining path
	// size, Multiple Service Packet's replies).
	Data []byte
}
```

CIPError reports a CIP response whose general status is not success. It keeps the service, the general status and the additional (extended) status words exactly as the peer sent them.

#### func (CIPError) Error

```go
func (e *CIPError) Error() string
```

Error describes the failure, for example "ethernetip: Get\_Attribute\_Single @1/1/9: attribute not supported (0x14)".

#### func (CIPError) ExtendedStatus

```go
func (e *CIPError) ExtendedStatus() (uint16, bool)
```

ExtendedStatus returns the first additional status word, and false when there is none.

#### func (CIPError) Is

```go
func (e *CIPError) Is(target error) bool
```

Is makes a CIPError with status 0x08 (service not supported) or 0x14 (attribute not supported) match ErrUnsupported.

### type ConnectionInfo

```go
type ConnectionInfo struct {
	// Class is the transport class (0, 1 or 3).
	Class uint8
	// OTConnID and TOConnID are the network connection IDs.
	OTConnID, TOConnID uint32
	// Serial, VendorID and OriginatorSerial identify the connection (its
	// connection triad).
	Serial           uint16
	VendorID         uint16
	OriginatorSerial uint32
	// OTRPI and TORPI are the actual packet intervals.
	OTRPI, TORPI time.Duration
	// Path is the connection path.
	Path cip.Path
	// Group is the multicast address of the T->O data, when it is
	// multicast.
	Group netip.Addr
}
```

ConnectionInfo describes a CIP connection for metrics and logs.

### type ContextLogger

```go
type ContextLogger interface {
	Logger

	DebugContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	InfoContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	WarnContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	ErrorContext(ctx context.Context, msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
}
```

ContextLogger extends [Logger](#type-logger) with context-aware structured logging, so that a handler can pick trace and span identifiers out of the context. When the Logger also implements ContextLogger, entries that belong to a request are logged with the context the request was called with.

### type FieldLogger

```go
type FieldLogger interface {
	Logger

	// With returns a logger that adds the given fields to every entry.
	With(keysAndValues ...any) FieldLogger

	DebugKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	InfoKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	WarnKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
	ErrorKV(msg string, keysAndValues ...any)
}
```

FieldLogger extends [Logger](#type-logger) with structured key-value logging. When the Logger given to a client or server also implements FieldLogger, the library logs through it: every entry is a constant message plus fields such as "component", "remote", "session", "connection" and "error", instead of one formatted string. [NewSlogLogger](#func-newsloglogger) returns such a logger.

keysAndValues alternate string keys and values, as in log/slog.

#### func NewSlogFieldLogger

```go
func NewSlogFieldLogger(h slog.Handler) FieldLogger
```

NewSlogFieldLogger is [NewSlogLogger](#func-newsloglogger) with the result typed as a [FieldLogger](#type-fieldlogger), for callers that want to add fields with With before handing the logger to a client or server. A nil handler returns a no-op logger.

### type Logger

```go
type Logger interface {
	Debugf(format string, args ...any)
	Infof(format string, args ...any)
	Warnf(format string, args ...any)
	Errorf(format string, args ...any)
}
```

Logger is the logging interface accepted by the client and the server. Implement it to integrate any logging library.

Logging is silent by default. Methods are invoked synchronously on the protocol path and must not block.

#### func NewSlogLogger

```go
func NewSlogLogger(h slog.Handler) Logger
```

NewSlogLogger wraps a slog.Handler. The result implements [FieldLogger](#type-fieldlogger) and [ContextLogger](#type-contextlogger), so the library logs structured fields through it; messages are only built when the handler is enabled for their level. A nil handler returns a no-op logger.

#### func NewStdLogger

```go
func NewStdLogger(l *log.Logger) Logger
```

NewStdLogger wraps a standard library logger. Each message is prefixed with its level. A nil l logs to os.Stderr with the standard flags.

#### func NopLogger

```go
func NopLogger() Logger
```

NopLogger returns a Logger that discards everything.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnConnect is called when a TCP connection is established (client)
	// or accepted (server).
	OnConnect(remote net.Addr)

	// OnDisconnect is called when a TCP connection ends. err is nil when
	// the application closed it.
	OnDisconnect(remote net.Addr, err error)

	// OnPacketSent is called after an encapsulation packet was written.
	// size is its length on the wire in octets.
	OnPacketSent(remote net.Addr, cmd encap.Command, size int)

	// OnPacketReceived is called for every encapsulation packet read.
	OnPacketReceived(remote net.Addr, cmd encap.Command, size int)

	// OnDecodeError is called when a packet, a common packet format or a
	// CIP message could not be decoded and was dropped or refused.
	OnDecodeError(remote net.Addr, err error)
}
```

Metrics is an optional callback interface for observing the sessions and the traffic of a client or a server. A nil Metrics disables collection.

The methods are called synchronously on the protocol path, possibly from several goroutines at once; implementations must be safe for concurrent use and must not block (increment a counter, send on a buffered channel).

Embed [NopMetrics](#type-nopmetrics) to implement only the callbacks you need and to stay compatible when methods are added.

### type RequestMetrics

```go
type RequestMetrics interface {
	// OnRequest is called before a request is sent.
	OnRequest(remote net.Addr, service cip.Service)

	// OnRequestDone is called with the outcome. err is nil on success;
	// classify failures with errors.Is and errors.As (*CIPError,
	// ErrTimeout, ...).
	OnRequestDone(remote net.Addr, service cip.Service, duration time.Duration, err error)
}
```

RequestMetrics is an optional extension of [Metrics](#type-metrics) for a client. When the value given to client.WithMetrics also implements it, the client reports every explicit request.

### type ServerMetrics

```go
type ServerMetrics interface {
	// OnHandled is called after an explicit request was handled, with its
	// general status.
	OnHandled(remote net.Addr, service cip.Service, status cip.GeneralStatus, duration time.Duration)

	// OnConnectionOpened is called after a Forward_Open succeeded.
	OnConnectionOpened(remote net.Addr, info ConnectionInfo)

	// OnConnectionClosed is called when a connection ends: by Forward_Close
	// (err nil), by timeout (ErrTimeout), with its session, or on Close.
	OnConnectionClosed(remote net.Addr, info ConnectionInfo, err error)
}
```

ServerMetrics is an optional extension of [Metrics](#type-metrics) for a server. When the value given to server.WithMetrics also implements it, the server reports every request it handled and every connection it opened, closed or lost.

### type State

```go
type State uint8
```

State is the state of a client's session or of an I/O connection.

```go
const (
	// StateDisconnected means there is no TCP connection, or the I/O
	// connection is closed.
	StateDisconnected State = iota
	// StateConnecting means the client is dialing and registering the
	// session, or the scanner is opening the I/O connection.
	StateConnecting
	// StateConnected means the session is registered, or the I/O
	// connection exchanges data.
	StateConnected
	// StateTimedOut means an I/O connection's consumed data stopped
	// arriving within the connection timeout.
	StateTimedOut
)
```

Session and connection states.

#### func (State) String

```go
func (s State) String() string
```

String returns "disconnected", "connecting", "connected" or "timed-out".
